object.title: Conlon's conjecture on norming graphs and stable reflection graphs
object.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph. A graph is **norming** if its associated graph norm is a norm, and a **stable reflection graph** is a graph arising as the specified $(G_1,G_2;G)$-graph, where $G$ is a finite reflection graph and $G_1,G_2$ are parabolic subgroups with $|G_1\cap G_2|=1$.

**Conlon's conjecture.** Every norming graph is a stable reflection graph. Equivalently, a graph is norming if and only if it is isomorphic to a special type of $(G_1,G_2;G)$-graph with these properties.

The conjecture proposes a complete correspondence between the functional-analytic property of being norming and a group-theoretic description; it would also imply the stated characterization using edge-transitivity under stable involutions. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
object.source_name: Joonkyung Lee and Alexander Sidorenko, “On graph norms for complex-valued functions”, arXiv:2101.12145 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.12145

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2021). “Since every norming graph is edge-transitive as proven in , the existence of a stable involution will prove the Polycirculant conjecture for line graphs of norming graphs in a strong sense, which adds plenty of examples to the conjecture.”

object.title: Normal rational curve completeness conjecture
object.statement:
Let $2\le N\le q-2$. In $\mathrm{PG}(N,q)$, a **normal rational curve** is a $(q+1)$-arc projectively equivalent to

$$
\{(1,t,t^2,\ldots,t^N):t\in\mathbb{F}_q\}\cup\{(0,\ldots,0,1)\}.
$$

A $(q+1)$-arc is **complete** if no further point can be added while preserving the arc property. **Normal rational curve completeness conjecture.** Every normal rational curve in $\mathrm{PG}(N,q)$ is a complete $(q+1)$-arc except when $q$ is even and $N\in\{2,q-2\}$, in which case one point can be added to the curve. This is a geometric formulation of the corresponding extremal-length question for MDS codes; the stated exceptions are precisely the cases in which an additional point may exist.
object.source_name: Alexander A. Davydov, Stefano Marcugini and Fernanda Pambianco, “On the weight distribution of the cosets of MDS codes”, arXiv:2101.12722 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.12722

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

object.title: The first prime-based upper-bound conjecture for domination in Knödel graphs
object.statement:
Let $KG_n$ be the Knödel graph on even $n$ vertices, and let $gamma(KG_n)$ denote its domination number. Let $p$ be an odd prime with $p\leq\lceil\log n\rceil$, and suppose that $2$ is a primitive root modulo $p$. **The first domination upper-bound conjecture.** It then follows that

$$
\gamma(KG_n)\leq\left\lceil\frac{n}{p}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture would relax the corresponding theorem's requirement that $p$ divide $n$; the expected dominating sets would use translations by the remainder of $n$ upon division by $p$.
object.source_name: Jesse Racicot and Giovanni Rosso, “Domination in Knödel Graphs”, arXiv:2102.00505 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.00505

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

object.title: The 5-coupled-choosability conjecture for IO-graphs
object.statement:
An **IO-graph** is a planar graph obtained by adding an independent set of vertices to the interior faces of an outerplanar graph. Every subgraph of a wheel is an IO-graph.

**IO-graph coupled-choosability conjecture.** Every IO-graph is 5-coupled-choosable.

This class lies between wheel subgraphs and planar partial 3-trees in the paper's investigation. The source does not provide a resolution of this conjecture, so its status remains open.
object.source_name: Sam Barr and Therese Biedl, “All Subgraphs of a Wheel are 5-Coupled-Choosable”, arXiv:2102.02918 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.02918

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2021). “But this does not imply 6-coupled-choosability of subgraphs, and so the conjecture remains open.”

object.title: Lando's degree conjecture for the \mathfrak{sl}_2 weight system on complete bipartite graphs
object.statement:
Let $K_{l,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $l$ and $n$, and let $w_{\mathfrak{sl}_2}$ denote the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ weight system.

**Lando's complete-bipartite reformulation.** The value of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ weight system at $K_{l,n}$ is a polynomial of degree $\min(l,n)$.

The paper presents this as a restatement of Lando's chord-diagram conjecture and verifies the cases with $l=1,2,3$ through explicit generating-function calculations. The general assertion remains open in the supplied text.
object.source_name: P. Filippova, “Values of the sl_2 weight system on complete bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2102.03487 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.03487

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

object.title: Dividing-edge conjecture for linear compartmental models
object.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a strongly connected linear compartmental model that is generically locally identifiable, with singular-locus equation $f$. An edge $j\to i$ is **dividing** if its parameter $k_{ij}$ divides $f$. **Dividing-edge conjecture.** If $j\to i$ is a dividing edge of $\mathcal M$, and the model $\mathcal{M}'$ obtained by deleting the edge $j\to i$ is strongly connected, then $\mathcal{M}'$ is unidentifiable. The conjecture is motivated by the converse of the known result that deleting non-dividing edges preserves generic local identifiability. It is proved in cases where deleting the edge increases the shortest input-output path length, but the general claim remains open.
object.source_name: Patrick Chan, Katherine Johnston, Anne Shiu, Aleksandra Sobieska and Clare Spinner, “Identifiability of Linear Compartmental Models: The Impact of Removing Leaks and Edges”, arXiv:2102.04417 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.04417

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2021). “However, this conjecture is false, as the next example shows.”

object.title: The finiteness conjecture for equal values of $P_m$ and $P_n$
object.statement:
Let $m,n\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ with $3\leq m<n$ and $(m,n)\neq(3,4)$. Consider the Diophantine equation

$$
P_m(x)=P_n(y).
$$

**Finiteness conjecture for $P_m$ and $P_n$.** This equation has only finitely many solutions in non-negative integers.

The conjecture is motivated by the paper's results on equal values of partition functions, with $(m,n)=(3,4)$ excluded because it is an exceptional case. The general finiteness assertion remains open.
object.source_name: Szabolcs Tengely and Maciej Ulas, “Equal values of certain partition functions via Diophantine equations”, arXiv:2102.05352 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.05352

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

object.title: Generalized niceness conjecture for subdivided complete bipartite graphs
object.statement:
Let $a,b,\ell,r$ be positive integers with $a\leq b$ and

$$
\frac{r}{r-1}\left(1-\frac{a-1}{a\ell}\right)\geq 1.
$$

Let $K_{a,b}^{\ell}$ denote the graph considered in the paper. **Generalized niceness conjecture.** Under these conditions, $K_{a,b}^{\ell}$ is $r$-nice. The conjecture proposes a further generalization of Theorem~; the paper notes that additional case analysis and new ideas are needed, and does not establish the claim in full.
object.source_name: József Balogh, Sean English, Emily Heath and Robert A. Krueger, “Lower bounds on the Erdős-Gyárfás problem via color energy graphs”, arXiv:2102.11466 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.11466

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

object.title: The 2-wqo one-point-extension conjecture for permutation classes
object.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a permutation class, and let $\mathcal{C}^{+1}$ denote its one-point extension. **The 2-wqo one-point-extension conjecture.** If $\mathcal{C}$ is 2-wqo, then $\mathcal{C}^{+1}$ is wqo. The assertion would follow from Pouzet's 2-wqo conjecture, since the proof in the source shows that every 4-wqo class has a wqo one-point extension; it also follows from the stronger conjecture that every 2-wqo class is lwqo.
object.source_name: Robert Brignall and Vincent Vatter, “Labelled well-quasi-order for permutation classes”, arXiv:2103.08243 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.08243

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2021).

object.title: Conjecture on Diophantine exponents of aperiodic episturmian words
object.statement:
Let $\mathbf{t}$ be an aperiodic episturmian word. Its **Diophantine exponent** is denoted by $\operatorname{dio}(\mathbf{t})$, and its partial quotients are those associated with its directive sequence.

**Diophantine-exponent conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{dio}(\mathbf{t})<\infty \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathbf{t}\text{ has bounded partial quotients}.
$$

This would extend the corresponding result for regular episturmian words to all aperiodic episturmian words. The claim is presented as a conjecture and remains open in the source.
object.source_name: Jarkko Peltomäki, “Initial nonrepetitive complexity of regular episturmian words and their Diophantine exponents”, arXiv:2103.08351 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.08351

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

object.title: Total domatic number conjecture for Cartesian products
object.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs without isolated vertices. For a graph $X$, let $d_t(X)$ denote its total domatic number, and let $G\mathbin\square H$ denote the Cartesian product of $G$ and $H$.

**Total domatic product conjecture.** One has

$$
d_t(G\mathbin\square H)\leq 2\max\{d_t(G),d_t(H)\}+1.
$$

The paper notes that examples such as $G=K_{2n+1}$ attain $d_t(G\mathbin\square G)=2d_t(G)+1$. The conjectured upper bound is presented as open; a weaker version using ordinary domatic numbers is also posed as an open problem.
object.source_name: P. Francis and Deepak Rajendraprasad, “On Domatic and Total Domatic Numbers of Product Graphs”, arXiv:2103.10713 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10713

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

object.title: Domatic number conjecture for Cartesian products
object.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs without isolated vertices. For a graph $X$, let $d(X)$ denote its domatic number, and let $G\mathbin\square H$ denote the Cartesian product of $G$ and $H$.

**Domatic product conjecture.** One has

$$
d(G\mathbin\square H)\leq 2\max\{d(G),d(H)\}+1.
$$

The source describes this as an open version of the total-domatic conjecture and states that, as far as the authors know, the corresponding conjecture for domatic number is also open.
object.source_name: P. Francis and Deepak Rajendraprasad, “On Domatic and Total Domatic Numbers of Product Graphs”, arXiv:2103.10713 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10713

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

object.title: Vajnovszki's equidistribution conjecture for descent and excedance bistatistics
object.statement:
Let $cmathfrak{S}_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements. A **bistatistic** is an ordered pair of permutation statistics, and two bistatistics are **equidistributed** if they have the same value distribution on $cmathfrak{S}_n$. The statistics $\operatorname{des}_2$ and $\operatorname{pex}$ denote descents of type $2$ and pure excedances, while $\operatorname{des}$ and $\operatorname{exc}$ denote descents and excedances.

**Vajnovszki's conjecture.** The two bistatistics $(\operatorname{des}_2,\operatorname{des})$ and $(\operatorname{pex},\operatorname{exc})$ are equidistributed on $cmathfrak{S}_n$.

The paper presents this as the second conjecture attributed to Vajnovszki. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Bin Han, Jianxi Mao and Jiang Zeng, “Equidistributions around special kinds of descents and excedances”, arXiv:2103.13092 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.13092

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

object.title: The symmetry conjecture for descent and ear statistics
object.statement:
For each $n$, let $cmathfrak{S}_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements, and let $\operatorname{des}_2$ and $\operatorname{ear}$ be the descent-of-type-$2$ and ear statistics on permutations. The distribution of a pair of statistics is **symmetric** when its associated bivariate generating polynomial is invariant under exchanging the two variables.

**Symmetry conjecture.** The distribution of $(\operatorname{des}_2,\operatorname{ear})$ over permutations is symmetric.

The source notes that related distributions are not symmetric in small cases, but speculates that the polynomial $P_n(x,y)=\sum_{sigma\incmathfrak{S}_n}x^{\operatorname{des}_2(sigma)}y^{\operatorname{ear}(sigma)}$ is invariant under $x\leftrightarrow y$.
object.source_name: Bin Han, Jianxi Mao and Jiang Zeng, “Equidistributions around special kinds of descents and excedances”, arXiv:2103.13092 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.13092

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

object.title: Best-case variance conjecture for the chromatic number of random graphs
object.statement:
Let $G_{n,p}$ be the binomial random graph with constant $p\in(0,1-1/e^2]$, let $Y_n=\chi(G_{n,p})$, and let $\sigma_n^2=\operatorname{Var}(Y_n)$. Define

$$
\widetilde w_n=\frac{n^{1/4}}{\log^{7/4}n}.
$$

**Best-case variance conjecture.** One has

$$
0<\liminf\frac{\sigma_n}{\widetilde w_n}<\infty.
$$

This is the proposed lower-order scale for the variance in the best case. The authors explicitly describe this conjecture as less certain than the worst-case statement and give no resolution.
object.source_name: Annika Heckel and Oliver Riordan, “How does the chromatic number of a random graph vary?”, arXiv:2103.14014 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14014

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

object.title: Frid's logarithmic palindromic-length conjecture for power-free words
object.statement:
Let $w$ be an infinite word, and let $\operatorname{PPL}_w(n)$ denote the palindromic length of the prefix of $w$ of length $n$. **Frid's conjecture.** If $w$ is $k$-power-free for some positive integer $k$, then

$$
\limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\operatorname{PPL}_w(n)}{\ln n}>0.
$$

This predicts logarithmic growth, along an infinite subsequence of prefix lengths, for the palindromic length of prefixes of every power-free infinite word.
object.source_name: Josef Rukavicka, “Palindromic Length and Reduction of Powers”, arXiv:2103.14609 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14609

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

object.title: The one-third–two-thirds conjecture for finite posets
object.statement:
Let $P=(X,\prec)$ be a finite poset, let $\operatorname{\mathcal{E}}(P)$ be its set of linear extensions, and write $e(P)=|\operatorname{\mathcal{E}}(P)|$. **The one-third–two-thirds conjecture.** If $P$ is not totally ordered, then there are distinct elements $x,y\in X$ such that

$$
\frac13\leq \frac{|\\{L\in\operatorname{\mathcal{E}}(P):L(x)<L(y)\\}|}{e(P)}\leq\frac23.
$$

This conjecture is open in full generality, although it is known for several special classes, including posets of width two, where the bounds are tight.
object.source_name: Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak and Greta Panova, “The cross-product conjecture for width two posets”, arXiv:2104.09009 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09009

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

object.title: Isometric dimension conjecture for braid graphs of reduced expressions
object.statement:
Let $(W,S)$ be a simply-laced triangle-free Coxeter system, and let ${\boldsymbol{\alpha}}$ be a reduced expression with link factorization

$$
{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}_1\mid {\boldsymbol{\alpha}}_2\mid\cdots\mid {\boldsymbol{\alpha}}_k.
$$

Write $B({\boldsymbol{\alpha}})$ for its braid graph, let $\dim_I$ denote isometric dimension, and let $\operatorname{rank}({\boldsymbol{\alpha}}_i)$ denote the rank of each link factor.

**Reduced-expression isometric-dimension conjecture.**

$$
\dim_I(B({\boldsymbol{\alpha}}))=\sum_{i=1}^k\operatorname{rank}({\boldsymbol{\alpha}}_i).
$$

This conjecture is presented as a consequence of the link dimension conjecture together with the product decomposition of braid graphs; it remains conditional and unproved in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Fadi Awik, Jadyn Breland, Quentin Cadman and Dana C. Ernst, “Braid graphs in simply-laced triangle-free Coxeter systems are partial cubes”, arXiv:2104.12318 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.12318

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

object.title: Goulden–Rattan square-coefficient inequalities for expanders
object.statement:
Let $Y_k(u)$ be the set of expanders with $k$ edges, $u-1$ white vertices and one black vertex. Let $X_k(i,j)$ be the set of expanders with $k$ edges, $i+j-2$ white vertices and two black vertices with weights $i-1$ and $j-1$. **Goulden–Rattan's square-coefficient conjecture.** For natural numbers $i\neq j$ and any natural number $k$,

$$
(2j-1)\left\|X_k(j,j)\right\|\geq (j-1)^2\left\|Y_k(2j)\right\|
$$

and

$$
(i+j-1)\left\|X_k(i,j)\right\|\geq 2(i-1)(j-1)\left\|Y_k(i+j)\right\|.
$$

These inequalities reformulate the Goulden–Rattan conjecture for square coefficients in terms of expanders. The supplied text does not state whether these inequalities have been proved or refuted, so their status remains open.
object.source_name: Mikołaj Marciniak, “Quadratic coefficients of Goulden-Rattan character polynomials”, arXiv:2104.13512 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.13512

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

object.title: Collins's matching peak conjecture for adjacency and distance polynomials of trees
object.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree. Let $CPA(T)$ and $CPD(T)$ denote the characteristic polynomials of its adjacency and distance matrices, respectively. Let $p_A(T)$ be the position of the peak of the absolute values of the non-zero coefficients of $CPA(T)$, and let $p_D(T)$ be the index of the peak of the normalized coefficients of $CPD(T)$. **Collins's conjecture.** The absolute values of the non-zero coefficients of $CPA(T)$ form a unimodal sequence, and its peak is at the same place as the peak of the normalized coefficients of $CPD(T)$.

The conjecture is presented as an open conjecture about the relationship between the two coefficient sequences for trees. The surrounding discussion gives supporting examples for paths and stars but does not establish the claim or provide a resolution.
object.source_name: Adam Zsolt Wagner, “Constructions in combinatorics via neural networks”, arXiv:2104.14516 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14516

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2021). “The conjecture regarding the location of the peak was disproved by Collins who showed that for paths the peak is at index approximately $\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right)n$.”
